content: 1. Cobicistat inhibits the metabolism of drugs processed by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to increased drug levels. Its use is contraindicated with certain medications. 2. Rifampin significantly reduces the levels and efficacy of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Rifapentine decreases darunavir levels by enhancing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Close monitoring is required, and alternative therapies should be considered. 4. Rifapentine also reduces cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 5. Darunavir increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 6. Darunavir elevates rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein transporter. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 7. Cobicistat also increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Darunavir raises riociguat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and reducing its clearance. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Monitor for hypotension and adjust the riociguat dose if necessary. 9. Cobicistat increases riociguat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for hypotension and adjust the riociguat dose if necessary. 10. Cobicistat elevates ripretinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Darunavir also increases ripretinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), raising the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 13. Cobicistat increases risperidone levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Co-administration of cobicistat with ritonavir is contraindicated due to increased levels of ritonavir via CYP3A4 inhibition. 15. Darunavir and ritonavir together increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Darunavir also raises ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 16. Ritonavir increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination requires close monitoring or alternative therapies. 17. Ritonavir elevates cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Darunavir increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Cobicistat also raises rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs due to the increased risk of bleeding. 20. Cobicistat increases roflumilast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Darunavir also elevates roflumilast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat increases romidepsin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 23. Darunavir also raises romidepsin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 24. Darunavir increases ropivacaine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Darunavir reduces rosiglitazone efficacy through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 26. Darunavir increases rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Cobicistat also raises rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 28. Rucaparib increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 29. Rucaparib also raises darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust CYP3A4 substrate dosages if clinically indicated. 30. Rufinamide reduces darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Cobicistat increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 32. Darunavir also elevates ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Reduce the starting dose of ruxolitinib to 10 mg BID with platelet counts ≥100 x 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 33. Darunavir increases salmeterol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of cardiovascular effects, including QT prolongation, palpitations, and sinus tachycardia. 34. Cobicistat also raises salmeterol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 35. Darunavir increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Limit saxagliptin to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Cobicistat also elevates saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 37. Darunavir increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Cobicistat also raises seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Cobicistat increases selexipag levels through mechanisms involving ABCG2 (BCRP). Monitor for increased pharmacologic or adverse effects when co-administered with ABCG2 inhibitors. 40. Cobicistat elevates selpercatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce selpercatinib dosage if co-administration is unavoidable. 41. Darunavir also raises selpercatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 42. Darunavir increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dosage and resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 43. Darunavir increases sertraline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust SSRI doses based on clinical assessment of antidepressant response. 44. Cobicistat also raises sertraline levels through mechanisms other than CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Darunavir increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. For erectile dysfunction, do not exceed sildenafil 25 mg every 48 hours. Chronic use for pulmonary arterial hypertension is contraindicated with cobicistat. 46. Darunavir increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 47. Cobicistat raises simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 48. Darunavir also elevates simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. 49. Cobicistat increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 50. Darunavir also raises siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors plus moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors is not recommended. 51. Darunavir increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Cobicistat also raises sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 53. Darunavir reduces sitagliptin efficacy through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 54. Darunavir increases topical sofpironium levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 55. Darunavir increases solifenacin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 56. Darunavir raises sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 57. Cobicistat also elevates sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 58. Darunavir increases sorafenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Darunavir and sparsentan together increase the toxicity of each other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 60. St. John’s Wort reduces darunavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of therapeutic failure and resistance development. 61. Darunavir increases stiripentol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, requiring monitoring of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates for increased or decreased effects.
